name: Sonified motion (the motion plays the score)

source.description: An inspected generative short (batch 1, 2026-11-26) states that every bounce plays the next note; its track measures as tonal, mid-band and without a bass bed, with onsets following the contacts rather than a tempo.

technique: Every physical event in the animation (a bounce, a collision, an arrival) triggers the next note of a pre-written melody, with bigger events getting bigger sounds. There is no separate music bed: the motion writes the soundtrack.
purpose: Perfect sync by construction; satisfying, toy-like feedback for simulations, algorithms and physics topics.
visual_behaviour: A ball bounces inside rings; each contact is a note; a ring breaking is a louder accent with a particle burst; the final escape is the biggest hit with a flash.
mechanics: Run a deterministic (seeded) simulation and log event frames with a kind (contact, break, finish). Map contact k to note k of a melody (pentatonic avoids clashes; pitch may step up with progress). Render notes with earshot sfx mallet or pluck (--pitch), place onsets on the event frames; a heavier sound for breaks; a release (swell plus hit) for the finish. Visual hierarchy matches: palette steps per stage, particles on breaks.

decomposition.timing: Event-driven; in the reference 64 onsets in 32 s, strongest 13-14 on ring breaks.

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Gain per event kind (contact < break < finish)

use_cases: algorithm and physics explainers (sorting, collisions, random walks)
data events as notes (each record, each step)
failure_modes: A non-deterministic simulation gives different notes per render
Notes too dense (> 8/s) turn into noise; thin the events or only sonify one kind
Contact sounds with long tails smear the rhythm

implementation.approach: Simulation stepped from the timeline time with a fixed dt and seeded PRNG (no requestAnimationFrame); event log exported to a cue file; audio rendered with earshot sfx render <mallet id> --pitch <note> per event and mixed at the cue frames (real-sfx mix.py).

additional_tooling.justification: earshot sfx (in the workspace) renders tuned mallet and pluck notes.

provenance.observed: The on-screen line says every bounce plays the next note; the track is 76% mid-band and tonal with no bass bed (tempo autocorrelation 0.18); the strongest onsets fall on the frames where a ring shatters into particles, and the largest on the final escape flash.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from a user-supplied reference (inspiration-only, rights unknown). Melodies and sounds are the project's own.
